overall: Tomorrow (Sunday, June 28) in Los Angeles is expected to be mostly sunny with mild temperatures near 70°F and light south-southeast winds of 5-10 mph. The wind advisory affecting inland desert areas expires at 5 AM PDT Sunday, so breezy conditions will be tapering off overnight into the morning. Marine influence appears to be keeping temperatures moderate and near-seasonal.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model disagreement, with GFS running as a significant warm outlier at ~84.3°F while NBM is the cool outlier at ~68.0°F. ECMWF (~75.0°F), HRRR (~77.4°F), and Weather.com (~73.8°F) cluster in a more coherent 73-77°F range, suggesting the ensemble mean of 74.5°F is better anchored than either extreme; the GFS warm signal deserves skepticism given the opposing consensus.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble model projects a TMAX near 74.5°F, broadly consistent with yesterday's observed 73.4°F and supported by the NWS narrative high of ~70°F. However, confidence is very low — the probability distribution is nearly flat across 68-81°F (Tier 4 Poor signals, even-bucket entropy 2.349, max bucket probability only ~20%), making precise bucket predictions unreliable. The weight of evidence favors the low-to-mid 70s, but significant uncertainty remains on both the warm (GFS) and cool (NBM) sides.
